description:
Continue the conversation in an interactive message. Partially evaluate roughly the next three useful turns: use what is already known to explain the situation, offer consequential proposals, and prepare the follow-ups each plausible answer would invite. The result should do useful thinking with the user, not merely survey preferences. An investigation or an editable proposal is a successful outcome; stop when the next step needs new evidence rather than inventing that evidence or extending an exhaustive questionnaire.

Separate observations from assumptions. Ground recommendations in the conversation or inspected material; mark unknowns and make proposed wording/plans editable with input defaults. Use markdown/text for substantive analysis, select for mutually exclusive directions and multi for compatible approaches the user may explore together. Put answer-specific continuations under exact option-text keys; each selected multi branch stays visible alongside the others. Prefer reveals for checked or selection-wide continuations, then when for cross-branch interactions. Approximate three turns by consequential depth, not a required number of questions. Defaults are proposals until Submit.

Classic widgets: text, markdown, slider, check, input (default/placeholder/rows), select, multi, rank (partial priority order), group and linear page. title is optional; omit redundant headings. Give options decision-relevant descriptions (because is an alias). multi.default accepts an option string or array. Exact option keys hold follow-up arrays; reveals appears while checked or once a selection exists. Conditions use bare ids, selected(id, value), count(id), any/all, comparisons, && || ! and parentheses; quote values containing a closing parenthesis. Hidden values read as unset even with defaults. References must exist; cycles including ancestor/descendant dependencies are rejected. If pages are needed, every top-level element is a page with Back/Next and one final Submit; page.when can skip steps.

Keep notes enabled. Every select/multi supplies Other (please specify) with free text automatically. Notes and unexpected answers can change the problem representation; explicit corrections override conflicting widgets. Ask only what still blocks progress. Use unique ASCII ids; avoid status, button, error, _notes, _labels, _route, __proto__, constructor, prototype and generated <id>_other_text collisions. Option values cannot collide with widget properties. Repair path-specific validation errors and retry. No page.next, conversation nodes, semantic routing, after_submit or intermediate submission exists.

Opening the tool returns awaiting_input with formId and definition, not a decision. Wait for the user message {"type":"popup_result","formId":"…","submissionId":"…","result":{…}}. Its terminal classic result is {"status":"completed","button":"submit","<id>":<value>,"_labels":{…},"_notes":"…"} or {"status":"cancelled"}. A repeated submissionId is duplicate delivery: do not repeat the action. Cancellation stops this question; do not reopen automatically. There is no backend answer storage.

Interpret the submitted evidence: absent keys were hidden or on unvisited pages; input "" is blank, select null unchosen, multi/rank [] empty, check false unchecked. Select returns option text; multi/rank return arrays (rank in priority order); slider returns a number; Other adds <id>_other_text. _labels explains ids and _notes adds instructions. Resume the original task from the actual answer, including corrections, without mistaking the opening acknowledgment or an unsubmitted default for agreement.

elements.markdown: Worked example — supplied fictional evidence: every matrix job repeats a 4-minute dependency install; integration tests take 18 minutes and share one database; the matrix covers Linux, macOS and Windows, but the release support policy has not yet been established.

Repeated installs are a plausible quick win. The 18-minute integration job is larger, but its shared database makes naive parallelism unsafe. Dropping platforms trades coverage for speed; I would preserve it until we know which platforms matter.

elements.multi: Which changes should we work through together?

options.description: Recover repeated install time; key the cache to the lockfile and runtime.
Attack the longest job after isolating its shared database.
Reduce matrix cost if the release support policy allows it.

Cache dependencies.default: Cache the package-manager download store by OS, runtime version and lockfile hash; keep immutable installs and leave the lockfile unchanged.

Cache dependencies.select: How should a changed lockfile behave?

options.description: A fresh key keeps invalidation simple; first run remains slow.
May save downloads; verify stale entries cannot bypass an immutable install.

Restore a nearby cache.markdown: I would restore only the download store, never installed dependencies, then compare a cold and warm run. A restore policy should earn its complexity with measured savings.

Restore a nearby cache.check: Benchmark restore fallback before adopting it

Parallelize integration tests.select: Can each worker own an isolated test database?

options.description: Partition by worker and clean up after each run before increasing concurrency.
Inspect fixtures and migration assumptions before promising faster tests.

Yes, isolate each worker.default: Create one disposable database per worker, run migrations once per database, and give each worker its own connection URL.

Not established — investigate first.markdown: The next useful step is to inspect global fixtures, database naming and cleanup, then report whether isolation is feasible. We cannot safely choose a worker count from the timings alone.

Not established — investigate first.check: Return an isolation proposal before changing test execution

options.description: Optimize elsewhere; current timings do not establish redundant coverage.
Keep the full release matrix; choose the smallest useful PR signal.

Reduce pull-request matrix only.input: Platform-specific risks that must stay covered
Reduce pull-request matrix only.placeholder: If unknown, inspect platform-dependent code before selecting exclusions

Reduce pull-request matrix only.input: Proposed PR coverage — edit or reject
Reduce pull-request matrix only.default: Run the fast representative checks on every PR; run the full supported-platform matrix before release. Verify native and filesystem-sensitive tests before reducing any PR coverage.

elements.markdown: With caching and test parallelism selected, benchmark them separately before combining them: faster installs should not conceal database contention. Reuse the same workload for cold/warm and one/two-worker comparisons.
elements.when: selected(changes, Cache dependencies) && selected(changes, Parallelize integration tests)
